reason: the correctness lens's findings the code or a test must fix

findings.text: correctness lens, medium: The pre-scan concludes 'all complete = all from prior iter' even when some members completed in the current interrupted iteration, causing build to be re-dispatched with stage.start when it should be skipped (DSCMBR-1 violated). (core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:1419; fix: code)

correctness lens, medium: The DSCMBR-1 test sets `stage_statuses.test = "aborted"` rather than `"complete"`, so the pre-scan's 'all complete' path (which fires when test has status "complete" from iter N-1 and build already completed in iter N) is never exercised; a future regression in that edge case would stay green. (tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh:276; fix: test)

correctness lens, low: The cycle-member artifact check inside the resume skip guard uses `"${_cyc_id//-/_}"` to build the `_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_*` var name, while the outer sanitisation for the jq key uses `"${_cyc_id//[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/}"` — two different transformations applied to the same `_cyc_id` within a few lines; a cycle ID with characters beyond `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` would look up the wrong var, missing member stages and silently skipping the artifact check. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:3608; fix: code)

correctness lens, low: The temporary `resume_mode=true` override used to skip persona preflight for `--from-stage` is applied before the auto-resume block; if the auto-resume block later resets `resume_mode=false` (e.g., because the state file reports `complete`), the final `--from-stage` validity check at line 2313 fires with `resume_mode=false` and rejects the run with a misleading message ('--from-stage is only valid with --resume') even though the user passed `--resume` explicitly. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:2026; fix: code)
